binders: A type Ω equipped with a measurable space.
An instance asserting that μ is a probability measure.
A real-valued function X : Ω → ℝ.
hypotheses: X is measurable from Ω to the Borel measurable space on ℝ.
conclusions: The μ-measure of {ω ∈ Ω | X(ω) ≥ t} is at most (∫⁻ ENNReal.ofReal(X(ω)) dμ) / ENNReal.ofReal(t).
mathematical_definitions: The threshold event is X⁻¹([t,∞)) = {ω ∈ Ω | t ≤ X(ω)}.
ENNReal.ofReal(r) is the extended-nonnegative-real embedding of the nonnegative part of r.
The numerator is the lower Lebesgue integral of ω ↦ ENNReal.ofReal(X(ω)) with respect to μ.
All quantities in the concluding inequality are extended nonnegative reals and may include ∞.
translation.proposition_plain_english: For every measurable space Ω, every measure μ on Ω satisfying the supplied probability-measure predicate, every measurable real-valued function X that is nonnegative μ-almost everywhere, and every positive real number t, the measure of the event on which X is at least t is no greater than the extended-nonnegative lower integral of the nonnegative part of X divided by the extended-nonnegative-real image of t.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: Nonnegativity is required only μ-almost everywhere, not at every point.
The threshold must be strictly positive; the proposition says nothing for t ≤ 0.
The event uses the closed upper interval [t,∞), so points where X(ω) = t are included.
No finiteness or integrability assumption is imposed on X; the lower integral and quotient may be ∞, in which case the inequality can be uninformative.

The integral explicitly uses ENNReal.ofReal(X(ω)), which clips negative values to zero; the almost-everywhere nonnegativity assumption identifies this with X in the intended nonnegative-integral interpretation except on a null set.
The proposition requires the IsProbabilityMeasure instance even though no normalization equation such as μ(Ω)=1 occurs explicitly in the displayed conclusion.
Because t > 0, ENNReal.ofReal(t) represents a positive finite denominator, assuming the conventional semantics of real numbers and ofReal.
ambiguities: The packet gives only the type, not the constructors or defining condition, of IsProbabilityMeasure; therefore the claim that it means μ(Ω)=1 is conventional rather than derivable from the supplied semantics.

The implementation body of lintegral is opaque (MeasureTheory.wrapped✝.1), so its identification with the standard lower Lebesgue integral cannot be independently reconstructed from this packet alone.

The internal definitions of MeasurableSpace, Measure, and Real are not exposed; their standard mathematical interpretations are indicated by their interfaces and uses but not fully derivable from the packet.
